models.name: Storm Intensity Distribution
models.description: Hybrid Normal-Pareto distribution for storm rainfall intensity modelling. Uses Gaussian core with Generalised Pareto Distribution (GPD) tail above a fitted threshold.
models.tier_rationale: Medium materiality: feeds into downstream hazard models but not directly into pricing. Medium complexity: hybrid distribution with threshold selection requiring expert judgement.
models.methodology: Hybrid Normal-GPD with maximum likelihood threshold estimation
models.methodology_rationale: Hybrid approach captures both typical and extreme rainfall. Pure Pareto overestimates body; lognormal underestimates tail. GPD-only misses the distribution body needed for moderate events.

assumptions.description: Storm events are independent
assumptions.monitoring: Check autocorrelation in residuals

assumptions.description: Stationarity of rainfall distribution
assumptions.monitoring: Rolling parameter stability test

assumptions.description: No spatial correlation between storm intensities
assumptions.monitoring: Cross-site correlation analysis

assumptions.description: GPD threshold selection is appropriate
assumptions.monitoring: Mean residual life plot stability

limitations.description: Independence assumption may not hold for clustered storm events
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Autocorrelation > 0.3 at lag 1

limitations.description: Stationarity assumption ignores climate change trends
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Significant trend in 10-year rolling parameters

limitations.description: No spatial correlation modelled
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Portfolio concentration in single catchment

limitations.description: Threshold selection involves subjective judgement
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Threshold sensitivity > 10% on tail quantiles

known_failure_modes: Very small sample sizes (<20 events) cause unstable GPD fit
Bimodal rainfall distributions (convective + frontal) poorly captured by single hybrid
Extreme extrapolation beyond observed data unreliable
models.input_data: Historical rainfall observations (Environment Agency gauge network)
models.output_data: Storm intensity probability distribution, exceedance probabilities

models.name: Storm-Gauge Response Model
models.description: Spatial decay model mapping storm intensity to gauge-level water levels. Uses distance-based attenuation with catchment-specific calibration.
models.tier_rationale: Medium materiality: translates storm events to local water levels for downstream GEV fitting. Medium complexity: spatial interpolation with calibrated decay parameters.
models.methodology: Spatial decay with distance-based intensity-to-level conversion
models.methodology_rationale: Physical decay model is interpretable and auditable. Kriging requires more data points than typically available. Neural networks lack transparency for regulatory purposes.

assumptions.description: No antecedent moisture conditions modelled
assumptions.monitoring: Compare predicted vs observed for wet/dry antecedent periods

assumptions.description: Linear storm track interpolation
assumptions.monitoring: Track reconstruction error analysis

assumptions.description: Static decay parameters
assumptions.monitoring: Parameter stability across seasons

assumptions.description: No tidal interaction
assumptions.monitoring: Residual analysis for coastal gauges

limitations.description: No antecedent conditions modelling
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Systematic under-prediction after prolonged wet periods

limitations.description: Linear track interpolation may miss curved storm paths
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Track error > 10km at gauge locations
limitations.compensating_control: Manual track review for significant events

limitations.description: Static sensitivity parameters
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Parameter drift > 15% over 12 months

limitations.description: No tidal interaction for coastal/estuarine gauges
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Prediction bias at tidal gauges
limitations.compensating_control: Exclude estuarine gauges or add tidal overlay

known_failure_modes: Gauges in urban areas with complex drainage may not follow spatial decay assumptions
Flash flood events with very localised intensity poorly modelled by regional decay
Snow-melt driven floods not captured by rainfall-only model
models.input_data: Storm intensity distribution (MKM-SI-001), gauge locations, catchment geometry
models.output_data: Per-gauge water level responses for each storm scenario

models.name: GEV Hazard Curve Model
models.description: Generalised Extreme Value distribution fitting for flood exceedance rates. Constructs hazard curves showing probability of exceeding given flood depths at each gauge location.
models.tier_rationale: High materiality: directly determines flood exceedance probabilities used in pricing and capital. High complexity: GEV fitting with shape parameter estimation, return level extrapolation, and term structure construction.
models.methodology: Maximum likelihood GEV fitting with exceedance rate scaling and return level term structure
models.methodology_rationale: GEV is the theoretically justified distribution for block maxima (annual maximum flood levels). GPD requires threshold selection; empirical methods cannot extrapolate; Log-Pearson less flexible shape.

assumptions.description: Annual maxima are independent and identically distributed
assumptions.monitoring: Ljung-Box test on annual maxima series

assumptions.description: Stationarity over the observation period
assumptions.monitoring: Mann-Kendall trend test on annual maxima

assumptions.description: Univariate analysis per gauge (no spatial dependence)
assumptions.monitoring: Cross-gauge correlation analysis

assumptions.description: Exceedance probability scaled by base flood rate
assumptions.monitoring: Base rate stability over time

limitations.description: Sample size sensitivity: <30 annual maxima gives unstable shape parameter
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Shape parameter confidence interval width > 0.3
limitations.compensating_control: Regional frequency analysis or Bayesian prior

limitations.description: Stationarity assumption may not hold under climate change
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Significant trend (p<0.05) in annual maxima

limitations.description: Univariate analysis ignores spatial flood dependence
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Correlated gauge failures in same event

known_failure_modes: Very short records (<15 years) produce unreliable extreme quantiles
Mixed flood generation mechanisms (pluvial + fluvial + tidal) violate iid assumption
Shape parameter > 0.5 indicates heavy tail that may be physically unrealistic
models.input_data: Per-gauge water level time series (from MKM-SG-001 or historical observations)
models.output_data: Hazard curves (exceedance probability vs flood depth), return levels, term structure

models.name: PRS Analytical Pricing Model
models.description: Analytical Physical Risk Swap spread calculation using hazard curve exceedance probabilities. Computes fair swap spreads for flood protection at gauge and property levels, with basis analysis.
models.tier_rationale: High materiality: directly determines PRS swap spreads used in trading and risk transfer. High complexity: credit-curve-style pricing with multiple depth thresholds, term structure, and basis waterfall decomposition.
models.methodology: Analytical spread from hazard curve exceedance rates with 5-component basis waterfall
models.methodology_rationale: Analytical approach is transparent, fast, and auditable. QuantLib CDS available as benchmark but adds dependency. Monte Carlo unnecessary for current product complexity. Simple expected loss ignores term structure.

assumptions.description: Zero recovery assumption on flood events
assumptions.monitoring: Compare with actual recovery rates when data available

assumptions.description: Flat risk-free curve
assumptions.monitoring: Interest rate curve steepness

assumptions.description: Quarterly discretisation of protection periods
assumptions.monitoring: Discretisation error vs monthly calculation

assumptions.description: No correlation between flood events at different properties
assumptions.monitoring: Portfolio-level concentration metrics

limitations.description: Zero-recovery assumption overstates spread for moderate floods
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Spread deviation from QuantLib benchmark > 20bps
limitations.compensating_control: Recovery rate overlay for moderate depth thresholds

limitations.description: Flat risk-free curve ignores term structure effects
limitations.monitoring_trigger: 2s10s curve steepness > 200bps

limitations.description: Quarterly discretisation introduces small pricing error
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Error vs monthly > 5bps

limitations.description: No correlation modelling between properties
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Portfolio HHI > 0.3

known_failure_modes: Very low exceedance probabilities (<0.01%) produce numerically unstable spreads
Basis waterfall can produce negative basis for highly concentrated portfolios
Short-term contracts (<1yr) may have insufficient premium to cover fixed costs
models.input_data: Hazard curves (from MKM-GH-001), property locations, depth-damage curves
models.output_data: PRS fair spread (bps), term structure of spreads, basis waterfall components

models.name: Depth-Damage Curve Model
models.description: Piecewise linear depth-damage functions mapping flood depth to property damage ratio. Supports multiple property types with calibrated damage curves.
models.tier_rationale: Medium materiality: determines damage ratios used in portfolio loss calculations. Low complexity: piecewise linear interpolation with published damage curves.
models.methodology: Piecewise linear interpolation from published depth-damage tables
models.methodology_rationale: Piecewise linear is transparent, matches published industry tables, and avoids overfitting. Polynomial fits can produce non-monotonic artifacts. ML approaches lack interpretability.

assumptions.description: Damage depends only on depth (not velocity or duration)
assumptions.monitoring: Compare with multi-factor models where data available

assumptions.description: Published damage curves are representative of UK properties
assumptions.monitoring: Actual loss data comparison when available

limitations.description: Single-factor model ignores velocity and duration effects
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Systematic bias in loss estimates for high-velocity flood zones
limitations.compensating_control: Velocity factor overlay for known high-flow areas

limitations.description: Curves based on published averages, not property-specific
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Predicted vs actual deviation > 20% for specific property types

known_failure_modes: Negative flood depths (basement flooding) not modelled
Very deep flooding (>3m) extrapolated beyond calibration range

remediation_steps.description: Validate depth-damage curves against JBA or Flood Re published curves
Add property-type-specific damage functions (residential vs commercial)

models.name: Spatial Interpolation Model
models.description: Inverse Distance Weighting interpolation for mapping gauge observations to property locations. Uses KDTree for efficient nearest-neighbour search with configurable power parameter.
models.tier_rationale: Low materiality: supporting calculation that maps gauge data to properties. Low complexity: well-established IDW algorithm with standard implementation.
models.methodology: Inverse Distance Weighting with KDTree nearest-neighbour search and Haversine distance
models.methodology_rationale: IDW provides smooth interpolation without requiring variogram estimation. Computationally efficient for real-time use. Kriging would require more gauge density than available.

assumptions.description: Spatial field is smooth between gauge locations
assumptions.monitoring: Cross-validation leave-one-out error

assumptions.description: Haversine distance is appropriate for distances < 50km
assumptions.monitoring: N/A - always valid at catchment scale

limitations.description: IDW cannot extrapolate beyond gauge network convex hull
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Properties outside gauge network

limitations.description: Isotropic weighting ignores terrain effects
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Large elevation differences between gauge and property

known_failure_modes: Properties very close to a single gauge get dominated by that gauge
Properties equidistant from gauges with very different readings produce averaged values
models.input_data: Gauge locations, gauge observations, property locations

models.name: Property Valuation Model
models.description: Factor-based property valuation using area, price/sqm, age, condition, flood risk, EPC rating, and proximity adjustments.
models.tier_rationale: Medium materiality: property values feed into LTV and damage calculations. Low complexity: multiplicative factor tables with published adjustments.
models.methodology: Multiplicative factor model: base_value x area_factor x age_factor x condition_factor x flood_factor x epc_factor x proximity_factor
models.methodology_rationale: Factor model is transparent and adjustable. Hedonic regression requires transaction dataset. ML models lack interpretability for regulatory purposes.

assumptions.description: Factor adjustments are multiplicative and independent
assumptions.monitoring: Interaction effects analysis

assumptions.description: Published factor tables are representative
assumptions.monitoring: Compare model values vs market transactions

limitations.description: No interaction effects between valuation factors
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Model vs market deviation > 15%

limitations.description: Factor tables may not reflect local market conditions
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Regional bias in residuals

known_failure_modes: Extreme property types (listed buildings, unusual construction) poorly captured
Rapid market movements not reflected until factor table update
models.input_data: Property attributes (area, age, type, condition, EPC, flood zone)

remediation_steps.description: Validate factor tables against Land Registry transaction data

models.name: Mortgage Pricing Model
models.description: Amortisation schedule with credit spread adjustment, LGD calculation, and expected loss present value for flood-exposed mortgages.
models.tier_rationale: Medium materiality: mortgage impairment calculations feed into portfolio risk. Medium complexity: amortisation with credit spread adjustment and LGD estimation.
models.methodology: Standard amortisation with flood-risk-adjusted credit spreads and LGD
models.methodology_rationale: Direct LGD calculation from flood damage is more transparent than structural models. Reduced-form requires default intensity calibration data not yet available.

assumptions.description: LGD equals max(0, outstanding - post_damage_value) / outstanding
assumptions.monitoring: Compare with actual recovery data when available

assumptions.description: Borrower continues payments unless in negative equity
assumptions.monitoring: Default correlation with LTV

limitations.description: No strategic default modelling
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Actual defaults below negative equity threshold

limitations.description: Single flood event assumption (no sequential events)
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Multiple events in same year

known_failure_modes: Interest rate changes not dynamically reflected in floating-rate mortgages
Property value recovery post-flood not modelled

models.output_data: Amortisation schedule, expected loss PV, post-damage LTV

models.name: Risk Analytics Model
models.description: Monte Carlo simulation engine for portfolio-level flood risk. Calculates VaR, Expected Shortfall, HHI concentration, and risk clustering across property portfolios.
models.tier_rationale: High materiality: VaR and ES metrics used in risk reporting and capital allocation. Medium complexity: standard Monte Carlo with well-known risk measures.
models.methodology: Monte Carlo simulation with scenario-based VaR, ES, and concentration metrics
models.methodology_rationale: Monte Carlo provides flexible scenario generation from storm catalogue. Historical simulation limited by available events. Parametric VaR too restrictive for fat-tailed flood losses.

assumptions.description: Storm scenarios are equally likely
assumptions.monitoring: Scenario probability validation

assumptions.description: Sufficient number of scenarios for stable quantile estimation
assumptions.monitoring: VaR convergence test

limitations.description: Equal probability assumption for all storm scenarios
limitations.monitoring_trigger: VaR instability across bootstrap resamples

limitations.description: No correlation between property losses within a scenario
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Actual correlated losses observed

known_failure_modes: Too few scenarios (<100) produce unstable tail quantiles
Concentrated portfolios may have insufficient scenario diversity
models.input_data: Storm scenarios, property portfolio, depth-damage curves
models.output_data: VaR, Expected Shortfall, loss distribution, HHI, clustering metrics

models.name: Delta Engine
models.description: PRS trade revaluation engine computing FS01 (Flood Sensitivity 01), mark-to-market, risky annuity, and portfolio risk grid aggregation. Uses numerical bump-and-reprice on the analytical PRS pricing model.
models.tier_rationale: High materiality: directly drives P&L, risk limits, and position management for the PRS trading desk. Medium complexity: standard bump-and-reprice approach using established pricing functions.
models.methodology: Numerical bump-and-reprice delta with quarterly risky annuity and yield-curve-matched discounting
models.methodology_rationale: Numerical delta via 1bp bump is standard practice for credit derivatives risk. Consistent with the discrete-time pricing model. Analytical delta would require separate derivation and maintenance.

assumptions.description: Parallel hazard rate bump for FS01 (no curve risk)
assumptions.monitoring: Compare FS01 prediction to actual revaluation P&L
assumptions.mitigation: Full revaluation available for P&L verification

assumptions.description: Constant basis for property trades under small gauge rate moves
assumptions.monitoring: Track basis stability vs gauge rate changes
assumptions.mitigation: Full basis recalculation for large moves

assumptions.description: Independent gauge moves (no cross-gamma)
assumptions.monitoring: Portfolio concentration limits by gauge

limitations.description: First-order sensitivity only; no gamma/convexity for large moves
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Unexplained P&L residual > 10% of daily P&L
limitations.compensating_control: Full revaluation check on material moves

limitations.description: No yield curve sensitivity (IR DV01)
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Yield curve moves > 50bp in a day
limitations.compensating_control: Yield curve is trader-controlled, moves are deliberate

limitations.description: No jump risk modelling for catastrophic events
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Hazard rate jump > 100bp intraday

known_failure_modes: Very high hazard rates (>10%) cause nonlinear spread behaviour not captured by 1bp bump
Zero-tenor trades (expired) return degenerate delta values
Missing market state file causes fallback to flat 4% rate
models.input_data: PRS trade files (CDM format), market_state.json (yield curve, hazard term structures)
models.output_data: Enriched trade records with MTM, FS01, fair spread, risky annuity; risk grid

remediation_steps.description: Add gamma (second-order sensitivity) computation for convexity monitoring

models.name: Flood Probability Classifier
models.description: Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM) classifier estimating per-gauge flood probability as a function of water level, storm hour, velocity, and acceleration: F(w,t,Δw,Δ²w) → P(flood). Trained on stress test vectors with time-decaying noise injection. v1.2 adds hydrograph derivative features (velocity, acceleration) enabling rising/falling asymmetry; AUC improved from 0.9189 to 0.9557.
models.tier_rationale: Medium materiality: feeds stress test P&L calculations for PRS trading desk. Medium complexity: GBM with hyperparameter tuning, per-gauge training, and noise-injected data regime.
models.methodology: Gradient Boosting Classification with binomial deviance loss
models.methodology_rationale: GBM provides probability calibration via sigmoid link, handles non-linear water level thresholds, and produces interpretable feature importances. Random Forest lacks native probability calibration; Logistic Regression cannot capture threshold non-linearity; Neural Network is overparameterised for four features; XGBoost adds unnecessary complexity for this feature space.

assumptions.description: Flood events are conditionally independent given water level and hour
assumptions.monitoring: Check residual autocorrelation across storms

assumptions.description: Four features (water level, hour, velocity, acceleration) are sufficient for classification
assumptions.monitoring: Track AUC stability across retraining; v1.2 improved AUC from 0.9189 to 0.9557
assumptions.mitigation: Feature expansion with upstream gauge levels or rainfall intensity

assumptions.description: Time-decaying noise is representative of operational uncertainty
assumptions.monitoring: Compare noise-injected vs clean-data AUC
assumptions.mitigation: Calibrate noise decay from operational forecast errors

assumptions.description: Alert-level threshold is the relevant flood definition
assumptions.monitoring: Review trigger levels annually

limitations.description: No spatial correlation between gauges modelled
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Correlated flood events missed in stress scenarios

limitations.description: Binary classification only — no severity estimation
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Stress P&L underestimates from ignoring flood depth
limitations.compensating_control: Conservative notional assumptions in P&L calculation

limitations.description: Training data generated from synthetic noise, not empirical forecast errors
limitations.monitoring_trigger: AUC divergence between synthetic and operational data

limitations.description: Stationarity assumed — no climate change adjustment
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Significant trend in flood frequency

models.name: Storm Sequence Generator
models.description: Multi-storm sequence generator implementing the insurance hours clause (168-hour event window). Produces catalogues of 1-5 related precipitation events (isolated, doublet, cluster, persistent) using budget-based window fitting, triangular duration/gap distributions, and correlated intensity sampling. v2.0 upgrade; replaces single-storm paradigm for stress testing. Trains stressm flood classifiers achieving mean AUC ~0.993.
models.tier_rationale: Medium materiality: primary training data source for stressm flood classifier (MKM-FC-001 v2.0) which feeds Portfolio Stress P&L. Medium complexity: sequence type selection, budget-based timing constraints, correlated intensity sampling within sequences.
models.methodology: Triangular distribution sampling with deterministic budget-cap and proportional gap scaling
models.methodology_rationale: Budget-cap + proportional gap scaling guarantees every sequence fits the event window in O(1) without rejection loops or fallbacks. Rejection sampling (v1.x) produced >20% fallback rate for catastrophic sequences corrupting the type distribution. Markov chains add unnecessary complexity for a training-data generator. Empirical catalogues are too sparse for 10,000-sequence batches.

assumptions.description: 168-hour event window matches reinsurance hours clause
assumptions.monitoring: Review against contract specifications annually
assumptions.mitigation: Window is configurable via EVENT_WINDOW_HOURS constant

assumptions.description: Budget cap distributes event window equally across all storms in a sequence
assumptions.monitoring: Track cap activation rate; flag if >50% of draws are capped
assumptions.mitigation: Recalibrate duration parameters if cap rate exceeds threshold

assumptions.description: Subsequent storm intensities are 70% likely to maintain or exceed the first storm (antecedent wetness proxy)
assumptions.monitoring: Compare simulated vs observed intensity correlation in multi-storm events
assumptions.mitigation: Adjust CORRELATION_PROB if empirical data available

assumptions.description: Triangular distributions adequately represent storm duration and gap variability
assumptions.monitoring: KS test of simulated durations against historical storm catalogue
assumptions.mitigation: Replace with empirically fitted distributions if KS p-value < 0.05

limitations.description: Budget cap truncates upper tail of duration distribution for high-intensity multi-storm sequences
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Cap activation rate > 50% for catastrophic category

limitations.description: Proportional gap scaling preserves relative spacing but not absolute minimums
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Scaled gaps < 1h in persistent catastrophic sequences
limitations.compensating_control: Minimum gap floor can be added if required

limitations.description: No spatial coupling between storms in a sequence (footprint, track unchanged)
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Portfolio stress scenarios show unrealistic spatial patterns
limitations.compensating_control: Spatial model (MKM-SG-001) applied independently per storm

limitations.description: Stationarity assumed; no climate change modulation of sequence frequency or intensity
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Significant trend in observed sequence frequency
limitations.compensating_control: Recalibrate SEQUENCE_PROBABILITY table if trends detected

known_failure_modes: Catastrophic 5-storm persistent sequences have >99% duration cap activation; generated storms are much shorter than physical reality
Gap scaling can compress persistent gaps to near-zero if catastrophic durations consume almost all budget
Intensity correlation model is symmetric; real compound events may show stronger escalation patterns
models.input_data: Intensity category weights and base intensity parameters (configured in batch_generator.py); catchment ID
models.output_data: List of StormSequence objects; storm_sequences.json; sequences_summary.json; gauge_summary.json

change_history.description: Initial release. Multi-storm sequence generator replacing single-storm paradigm. Four sequence types (isolated/doublet/cluster/persistent), budget-based window fitting, correlated intensity sampling. Downstream stressm classifier achieves AUC ~0.993.

models.name: Gauge Historical Daily
models.description: Synthetic daily water level generation with tidal influence, AR(1) autocorrelation, seasonal cycles, and Poisson flood injection
models.tier_rationale: Medium materiality: generates synthetic historical daily water levels used for backtesting and calibration. Medium complexity: AR(1) process with seasonal components, tidal harmonics, and Poisson-driven flood event injection.
models.methodology: AR(1) stochastic process with seasonal mean, tidal harmonics, Gaussian noise, and Poisson flood injection
models.methodology_rationale: AR(1) with seasonal decomposition provides physically interpretable parameters (autocorrelation, tidal amplitude, flood rate) while remaining computationally efficient for daily generation across 40 gauges. ARIMA adds unnecessary differencing for stationary gauge levels. Empirical resampling cannot generate novel flood events. HMM overparameterised for this use case.

assumptions.description: Daily water levels follow a stationary AR(1) process with seasonal mean
assumptions.monitoring: Check residual autocorrelation and seasonal decomposition stability

assumptions.description: Tidal influence is adequately captured by sinusoidal harmonics
assumptions.monitoring: Compare generated tidal patterns against observed tide tables

assumptions.description: Flood events arrive as a Poisson process independent of water level
assumptions.monitoring: Check flood clustering in generated series
assumptions.mitigation: Add state-dependent flood rate if clustering detected

assumptions.description: Gaussian noise adequately represents non-tidal variability
assumptions.monitoring: QQ plot of residuals against normal distribution
assumptions.mitigation: Switch to Student-t or empirical noise distribution

limitations.description: No spatial correlation between gauges in daily generation
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Cross-gauge correlation in generated series deviates from observed
limitations.compensating_control: Independent generation per gauge; spatial effects captured downstream

limitations.description: Poisson flood injection may not capture compound event clustering
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Observed multi-day flood events not reproduced
limitations.compensating_control: Flood duration parameter extends events beyond single day

limitations.description: Stationarity assumed; no climate trend in baseline levels
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Significant trend in observed annual mean water levels

known_failure_modes: Very high AR(1) coefficient (>0.98) can produce unrealistic drift
Poisson rate too high generates implausibly frequent flood events
Tidal amplitude miscalibration produces unphysical negative water levels
models.input_data: Gauge metadata (baseline level, tidal range, flood thresholds) from gauge.json
models.output_data: Daily water level time series per gauge in gaugehd/ directory

models.name: Stress Test Pipeline
models.description: End-to-end stress testing orchestration: storm sequences, seasonal baselines, compound gauge responses, and GBM classifier training
models.tier_rationale: High materiality: orchestrates the full stress testing pipeline feeding trading desk P&L scenarios. High complexity: multi-stage pipeline combining storm generation, gauge response simulation, seasonal adjustment, and classifier training.
models.methodology: Multi-stage pipeline: storm sequence generation, seasonal baseline computation, compound gauge response simulation, and GBM classifier training with balanced sampling
models.methodology_rationale: Modular pipeline with explicit stage handoffs provides auditability and reproducibility required for stress testing governance. Monolithic script lacks stage isolation for debugging. Event-driven adds unnecessary infrastructure complexity. Map-reduce parallelism not needed for current portfolio size.

assumptions.description: Storm sequences are representative of plausible multi-event scenarios
assumptions.monitoring: Compare generated sequence statistics against historical catalogues

assumptions.description: Seasonal baselines adequately capture gauge-level background water levels
assumptions.monitoring: Compare seasonal profiles against observed daily means
assumptions.mitigation: Update seasonal parameters from latest gaugehd data

assumptions.description: Compound gauge responses are additive over storm sequences
assumptions.monitoring: Check for non-linear interaction effects in multi-storm responses
assumptions.mitigation: Add interaction terms if significant non-linearity detected

assumptions.description: Balanced sampling (alert + sub-alert) produces unbiased classifiers
assumptions.monitoring: Track class balance and AUC stability across retraining
assumptions.mitigation: Adjust sampling ratio if class imbalance affects AUC

limitations.description: Pipeline runs sequentially; no concurrent gauge processing
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Pipeline runtime exceeds SLA for portfolio size > 100 gauges

limitations.description: No feedback loop from classifier performance to storm generation
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Classifier AUC degrades below 0.90
limitations.compensating_control: Manual review and recalibration if AUC drops

limitations.description: Stationarity assumed across pipeline stages
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Significant trend in flood frequency or severity
limitations.compensating_control: Annual full pipeline rerun with updated parameters

known_failure_modes: Missing gauge metadata causes pipeline stage to skip gauge silently
Insufficient alert-level storms in catalogue causes imbalanced training data
Large storm catalogues (>50,000) may exhaust memory during balanced sampling

models.name: Property Flood Response
models.description: Property-level flood depth estimation, depth-damage curves, spatial interpolation, velocity modelling, and portfolio risk analytics
models.tier_rationale: High materiality: directly computes property-level flood losses feeding portfolio VaR and insurance premium calculations. High complexity: integrates spatial interpolation (IDW/KDTree), depth-damage curves, Manning's velocity equation, hydrograph attenuation, and Monte Carlo risk analytics.
models.methodology: Multi-component flood risk framework: IDW spatial interpolation, piecewise-linear depth-damage curves, Manning's equation velocity model, exponential attenuation, and Monte Carlo portfolio analytics
models.methodology_rationale: IDW interpolation with depth-damage curves provides physically interpretable property-level estimates at computational cost suitable for portfolio-scale Monte Carlo. Full 2D hydraulic modelling is computationally prohibitive for 200+ properties. Binary models lose damage severity information. ML damage prediction lacks interpretability for governance. Copula spatial dependence adds complexity without clear benefit for current portfolio density.

assumptions.description: IDW interpolation adequately represents flood depth spatial variation between gauges
assumptions.monitoring: Compare interpolated depths against observed flood footprints
assumptions.mitigation: Increase gauge density or switch to kriging if IDW proves inadequate

assumptions.description: Depth-damage curves are transferable across property types
assumptions.monitoring: Compare predicted vs observed losses by property type
assumptions.mitigation: Develop property-type-specific curves if significant divergence

assumptions.description: Manning's equation is appropriate for urban flood velocity estimation
assumptions.monitoring: Validate velocities against 2D model outputs where available
assumptions.mitigation: Calibrate Manning's n coefficient per land use type

assumptions.description: Exponential attenuation captures distance decay of flood impact
assumptions.monitoring: Check attenuation curves against topographic analysis
assumptions.mitigation: Replace with terrain-based attenuation if DEM data available

limitations.description: IDW does not account for topographic barriers or flow paths
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Properties behind flood defences show predicted flooding
limitations.compensating_control: Manual review of properties near flood defences

limitations.description: Depth-damage curves assume instantaneous damage; no duration dependence
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Prolonged flooding causes higher losses than predicted

limitations.description: No building-level vulnerability modelling (construction type, floor level)
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Systematic over/under-prediction for specific building types
limitations.compensating_control: Property type categorisation in depth-damage curves

limitations.description: Monte Carlo convergence depends on sample size; may be slow for large portfolios
limitations.monitoring_trigger: VaR estimate instability with current sample size
limitations.compensating_control: Convergence diagnostics and adaptive sample sizing

known_failure_modes: Properties equidistant from multiple gauges may show averaged rather than realistic flood depths
Extreme extrapolation beyond observed gauge levels produces unreliable depth estimates
KDTree lookup fails gracefully but silently for properties outside gauge network coverage
models.input_data: Property locations and metadata (property.json), gauge levels and locations (gauge.json), storm responses (gaugets/)
models.output_data: Property flood depths, damage estimates, portfolio VaR/ES, insurance premiums, risk scores

models.name: Flood Polynomial Model
models.description: Logistic sigmoid with quadratic polynomial kernel approximating the GBM flood classifier. Maps log-space water level ln(w/s) and storm time ln((t+1)/T) to P(flood) via six fitted coefficients. R²=0.94 against the full GBM surface. Used for portfolio stress (time-independent variant) and single-gauge stress scenarios.
models.tier_rationale: Low materiality: approximation of existing GBM classifier for portfolio-level stress. Low complexity: closed-form logistic sigmoid with 6 fixed coefficients, no training required.
models.methodology: Nonlinear least-squares fit of logistic sigmoid to GBM probability surface
models.methodology_rationale: Quadratic sigmoid captures the essential water level × time interaction with only 6 parameters. Linear interpolation loses the time dimension; step functions create discontinuities; cubic adds marginal accuracy (MAE 0.033 vs 0.046) with more parameters; full GBM requires per-gauge trained models which are not always available.

assumptions.description: Coefficients fitted from a single gauge are generalizable across gauges
assumptions.monitoring: Compare polynomial P(flood) vs GBM P(flood) across multiple gauges
assumptions.mitigation: Refit coefficients on a panel of gauges if cross-gauge error exceeds 10%

assumptions.description: Quadratic polynomial is sufficient to approximate the GBM decision surface
assumptions.monitoring: Track R² and MAE against GBM surface at each retraining cycle
assumptions.mitigation: Upgrade to cubic polynomial if R² drops below 0.90

assumptions.description: Delta features (velocity, acceleration) can be ignored without material loss of accuracy
assumptions.monitoring: Compare polynomial predictions against 4-feature GBM at steady-state (Δw=0)
assumptions.mitigation: Add derivative interaction terms if steady-state assumption proves inadequate

limitations.description: Fitted from a single gauge (GAUGE-dc5e88fb) — may not generalize to all catchments
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Cross-gauge MAE exceeds 0.10 against GBM baseline
limitations.compensating_control: Use full GBM classifier where trained models are available

limitations.description: Does not capture gauge-specific behaviour (catchment shape, response time)
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Systematic bias for specific gauge types (tidal, flashy, regulated)
limitations.compensating_control: Manual review of polynomial vs GBM divergence during stress reporting

known_failure_modes: Extrapolation beyond the fitted water level range may produce implausible probabilities
At extreme early hours (hour 0-2), the polynomial may diverge from GBM predictions

key_parameters.name: a (log_h_s)
key_parameters.description: Coefficient for log water level h = ln(w/s)

key_parameters.name: b (log_t)
key_parameters.description: Coefficient for log storm time t = ln((hour+1)/168)

key_parameters.name: c (h*t interaction)
key_parameters.description: Coefficient for water level × time interaction

key_parameters.name: d (h² quadratic)
key_parameters.description: Coefficient for quadratic water level term

models.input_data: Water level (m AOD), storm hour index, severe flood threshold (m AOD) per gauge

remediation_steps.description: Validate polynomial predictions against GBM on at least 10 additional gauges

models.name: Building Resilience Index (BRI) Model
models.description: Property resilience assessment with two co-located outputs: (1) BRI letter rating (AA / AA+ / A / A+ / B / B+ / NR) derived via weakest-link aggregation across applicable hazards from a 5-level resilience checklist, and (2) Flood resilience score (1-100) per the IFC BRI Resilience Function Specification — a weighted 13-measure model with regime multipliers, soft caps, and a linear damage modifier intended to scale an existing flood damage function.
models.tier_rationale: Medium materiality: produces resilience ratings and scores that feed downstream consumers (governance reporting, insurance ratings, future damage-function scaling) but does not currently enter pricing directly. High complexity: two related-but-distinct scoring paradigms (categorical weakest-link letter rating + continuous weighted-measure score with soft caps), Thames-specific calibrated weights, 13-measure compliance mapping with mixed continuous/ordinal/binary inputs, regime-specific weight multipliers.
models.methodology: Two co-located methodologies. (1) BRI letter rating: per-hazard score from 5-level resilience checklist (Not assessed=0, Partial=0.4, Meets minimum=0.7, Enhanced=0.9, Verified=1.0) weighted by section + per-field weights; overall letter is weakest-of applicable hazards with '+' modifier when ContinuityMeasures section score >= 0.65. (2) Flood resilience score: per-spec 13 weighted measures (sum to 100), regime-specific weight multipliers (pluvial / fluvial / coastal), four soft-cap rules, linear damage modifier M(S,r) = 1 - alpha_r * (S-1)/99 with alpha = {0.65, 0.60, 0.50}.
alternatives_considered: Pure weakest-link letter rating only (rejected: loses score granularity for portfolio analytics)
Continuous score only without letter rating (rejected: letter scale needed for human-readable disclosure)
Single-paradigm hybrid where letter is derived from score thresholds (deferred: requires calibration data not yet available)
Per-property location-context normalisation (deferred: design under review)
models.methodology_rationale: The letter rating mirrors IFC BRI public methodology and produces an auditable, disclosable grade. The continuous score provides the precision needed for loss-given-hazard scaling and portfolio aggregation. Co-locating them in one module gives a single source of truth for resilience analytics. Thames-specific weights reflect the dominant fluvial flood hazard in the catchment; other catchments would have their own copy.

assumptions.description: Resilience checklist 5-level enum is interpretable consistently across assessors (Not assessed / Partial / Meets minimum / Enhanced / Verified)
assumptions.monitoring: Inter-rater agreement studies on a sample portfolio
assumptions.mitigation: Reference photos and worked examples per measure; assessor calibration training

assumptions.description: Section and per-field weights (Flood 30%, Site/Drainage 25%, Building 20%, Continuity 15%, Fire 10%) are appropriate for Thames flood-dominant risk
assumptions.monitoring: Sensitivity analysis on weight perturbations >= +/- 10%
assumptions.mitigation: Re-tune via recalibrate_thresholds_from_scores() when loss data is available

assumptions.description: Weakest-link aggregation across hazards is appropriate; ignoring non-applicable hazards (HazardClass = None) is appropriate
assumptions.monitoring: Compare weakest-link vs. weighted-average overall ratings on a sample
assumptions.mitigation: Switch to weighted average if downstream consumers prefer smoother grades

assumptions.description: Flood-spec 13-measure weights (sum to 100) reflect the relative damage-reduction contribution of each measure under flood conditions
assumptions.monitoring: Validate against published flood damage attribution studies
assumptions.mitigation: Recalibrate weights when claims/engineering loss data available; spec author flagged these as 'first implementation, not final scientific calibration'

assumptions.description: Flood regime mapping (Fluvial / Pluvial / GroundWater / Coastal / Multiple to pluvial/fluvial/coastal alpha values) is appropriate
assumptions.monitoring: Review regime classification accuracy against catchment hydrology
assumptions.mitigation: Re-map if regime classification proves unreliable

assumptions.description: Linear damage modifier M(S,r) = 1 - alpha_r * (S-1)/99 captures the mitigation effect adequately
assumptions.monitoring: Validate vs. observed mitigated-vs-unmitigated loss ratios
assumptions.mitigation: Switch to a non-linear modifier (e.g. exponential) if linear under- or over-corrects

assumptions.description: Spec measure -> CDM field bindings reflect the engineering intent of each spec measure, including the four proxy mappings (water_resistant_materials -> PermanentFloodProofingAtEntries, debris_impact_resistance -> OpeningsWindResistant, roof_drainage_standard -> RoofRatedForDesignWind, roof_membrane_openings_seal -> RoofEdgeDetailWindResistant)
assumptions.monitoring: Recalibrate proxy measures when loss data attributes residual damage to misaligned controls
assumptions.mitigation: Add dedicated CDM fields for the four proxied measures if needed

limitations.description: Score distribution is currently bell-centred (mean ~58, median ~57) rather than the design-target right-skewed shape (heavy left tail of low-quality stock)
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Coarse skew check: low-quality (<30) fraction stays below 20%
limitations.compensating_control: Adjust generator priors or compliance credit mapping; document the design intent vs. observed shape

limitations.description: No location/hazard-context normalisation: a Zone 1 property and a Zone 3b property with identical measures receive identical scores. The IFC BRI methodology supports context-normalisation but it is not yet implemented here
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Comparison of Zone 1 vs. Zone 3 mean scores at matched measure compliance
limitations.compensating_control: Use FloodHazardClass alongside the score for downstream consumers; design under review

limitations.description: Damage modifier M(S, r) is computed but not yet wired into the existing flood damage function (LGH_adj = BaselineDamage x M)
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Damage function consumers do not consume the modifier
limitations.compensating_control: Phase 2 integration with src/models/floodrisk/depth_damage when calibration data available

limitations.description: Four spec measures use proxy CDM fields (BRI-A7) — they may bias the score in either direction for properties with strong wind-rating but weak water-tightness or vice versa
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Residual loss attribution to proxy measures > 15% in claims data
limitations.compensating_control: Document proxy use; add dedicated CDM fields when calibration justifies

limitations.description: Thames-specific calibration (weights, thresholds, regime defaults) does not generalise to other catchments without re-tuning
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Application of MKM-BRI-001 to non-Thames properties
limitations.compensating_control: Per-catchment copy of resilience.py with catchment-specific weights when other catchments are onboarded

limitations.description: Confidence score component of the spec (verification, evidence quality, recency, completeness) is not yet implemented
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Downstream consumers ask for confidence-weighted scores
limitations.compensating_control: Implementation deferred; can be added without breaking the score outputs

known_failure_modes: All-Verified resilience checklist produces score near 100 — unrealistic if no real-world property scores that high; soft caps mitigate but do not eliminate
Properties with HazardClass = None across all hazards produce overall rating from fallback weighted score path, which differs subtly from the weakest-link path
FloorLevelMeters set to 0 or below triggers the lowest_occupied_floor_elevation soft cap at 40 — correct behaviour but coarse
RegimeMultipliers + soft caps interact non-trivially: a property in pluvial regime with both retainage and drainage at 0 is capped at 55 regardless of other strengths
PropertyID-keyed jitter RNG for the non-flood hazard scores means scores are deterministic for a given PropertyID but two properties with the same flood score get different sibling scores
key_parameters: FLOOD_SPEC_BASE_WEIGHTS (13 spec measure weights, sum to 100)
models.input_data: PropertyHeader (PropertyPeriod, PropertyCondition, EAFloodZone, BasementPresent, FloorLevelMeters, FloodRiskType); ProtectionMeasures.ResilienceMeasures (5 sub-sections of 5-level checklists); ProtectionMeasures.HazardProfile (FloodHazardClass, WindHazardClass, FireHazardClass, SeismicHazardClass); HistoryAndIncidents.FloodEvents.FloodDamageSeverity.
models.output_data: ProtectionMeasures.RiskAssessment.GoverningBodyRatings fields: BRIRating (letter), BRIScore (mean of hazard scores), BRIFloodRating/BRIWindRating/BRIFireRating/BRISeismicRating (per-hazard letters), BRIFloodScore (flood-spec score 0-1) plus jittered siblings BRIWindScore/BRIFireScore/BRISeismicScore, BRIDate/BRIRatingVersion/BRIRatingAgent (metadata). Damage modifier returned by apply_flood_resilience_score but not persisted.
